findings.title: The `http:`/`https:` scheme guard in parseAllowlistEntry is asserted by no test — all four fixtures are caught by the PATH guard instead
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Confirmed non-equivalent by inspection. All four fixtures have a non-empty, non-'/' pathname (file:///etc/passwd -> '/etc/passwd', data:text/html,<script> -> 'text/html,<script>', blob:https://admin.example/1234 -> 'https://admin.example/1234', javascript:alert(1) -> 'alert(1)'), so with the scheme throw deleted every one still throws AdminOriginConfigError from the path throw two guards later. The mutant is observably different: readAdminAppOrigins() returns ['ftp://admin.example'] / ['null'] instead of throwing for entries whose pathname is '/' (ftp://, ws://, wss://, file://host) — that is an exported-function behaviour change, so 'equivalent' cannot be claimed. Not an unexecuted branch: the test DOES run the scheme guard, its assertion simply cannot distinguish which guard fired. Security impact is nil today because normalizeOrigin independently enforces http(s) on the request side, so no extra origin becomes admissible; the defect is in the ORACLE. One-line fix: add an entry whose ONLY disqualifier is the scheme (e.g. 'ftp://admin.example' or 'ws://admin.example') to the fixture list.

findings.title: The Edge-safety guard's `node:` entry can never match, and side-effect imports are invisible — both node-builtin import shapes survive

The membership test is `s === bad || s.startsWith(`${bad}/`)`; for bad='node:' that demands the specifier be exactly 'node:' or start with 'node:/', neither of which is a real specifier, so 'node:crypto' passes (M27 survived). Separately the extractor is /from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g, so a bare `import 'node:crypto';` yields no specifier at all (M28 survived). The 'node builtins' third of the test's stated property is enforced by nothing, which is the exact hole the cited precedent (src/lib/auth/__tests__/admin-transport.test.ts:114-119) documents a prior red-team pass walking through twice. The '@/lib/db', 'postgres', 'bullmq', 'openai', '@anthropic-ai/sdk', '@supabase/supabase-js' and 'ioredis' entries DO match and are unaffected. No live defect: the graph carries no node: import at HEAD. Fix: special-case the scheme (s.startsWith('node:')) and widen the extractor to /(?:from|import)\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g.

findings.title: Fix 1's fail-closed fallback keys on VERCEL, which Vercel documents as the marker that system environment variables ARE exposed - so in the exact configuration A1 describes the predicate still returns false
findings.arbiter_reasoning:
Duty 3, re-resolved this pass against vercel.com/docs/environment-variables/system-environment-variables via the Vercel documentation MCP: 'VERCEL environment variable - Indicates that system environment variables are exposed to the deployment. VERCEL=1'. VERCEL is itself a system environment variable and its documented meaning is that the exposure toggle is ON. A1's scenario is a project whose system variables are NOT exposed; there VERCEL_TARGET_ENV is absent AND VERCEL is absent, so process.env.VERCEL !== undefined is false and isProductionEnvironment() returns false - http://localhost:<any port> stays admissible on a real production deployment, which is the hole the fix was written to close. Two consequences, both checked. (a) NO REGRESSION: the new predicate returns exactly what the old one returned in every configuration where the fallback runs, and R14/R15/R16/R17 all killed, so the shipped behaviour is unchanged and correctly pinned. (b) The CLAIM is what fails: the JSDoc at src/lib/config/flags.ts:57-62 ('on Vercel with the signal switched off - treat as production') and triage.md:37's A1 disposition both assert a property the marker cannot deliver. Rated P1 not P0 because the evidence is vendor documentation rather than a probe of this project's own deployment, and because nothing regressed. Blast radius checked and small: isAllowedAdminOrigin's loopback clause (src/lib/config/admin-origins.ts:188) is the ONLY caller in the repo. Local dev, pnpm test and the Railway worker are unaffected - VERCEL is unset in all three, and the repo runs next dev, never vercel dev (no occurrence of 'vercel dev' outside node_modules). Remedy: verify live the way src/lib/config/deployment-lane.ts:5-10 verified the Railway signals ('Verified live against Railway on 2026-07-28'), or key the fallback on something that survives the toggle. If this project's toggle is ON - the default - the fallback is dead code and A1 was hypothetical here; say that instead of claiming a fix.

--- ORCHESTRATOR TRIAGE (post round 2) ---
FIXED at 1ded393a+1. The fallback no longer keys on VERCEL — which is itself a system environment variable meaning 'system variables ARE exposed', so it is absent in exactly the configuration the fallback exists for. It now keys on NODE_ENV === 'production', which is true on every Vercel build, so the A1 hole is genuinely closed. The imprecision (staging builds also set NODE_ENV=production) is reached ONLY when VERCEL_TARGET_ENV is missing and errs toward DENYING loopback; an affirmative target still beats it, which the new test cases pin (staging + preview under NODE_ENV=production stay non-production).

Second, smaller point: isProtectedOwnerApiRoute and isProtectedMixedRoleApiRoute both call normalizePath on their argument, isAdminApiRoute does not (its JSDoc says so), so an external caller passing '/API/Admin/x' gets false. Both call sites normalize today, so that is a shape note, not a defect. src/lib/shared/__tests__/protected-routes.test.ts is inside allowed_edit_surface.

--- ORCHESTRATOR TRIAGE (post round 2) ---
FIXED. protected-routes.test.ts gained four isAdminApiRoute cases in its own suite: the matched surface, lookalike prefixes, the already-normalized-input contract stated as a test rather than a comment, and agreement with isProtectedRoute.

findings.title: The catch's non-AdminOriginConfigError rethrow is unreachable at HEAD and exercised by no test

--- ORCHESTRATOR TRIAGE (post round 2) ---

Swallowing an unexpected error into a 403 origin would hide a real fault behind a CORS refusal. Being unmeasured is the correct condition for an assertion that must never fire.
findings.reason: Kept deliberately: the unreachable rethrow is the 'assert impossible states' rule, not defensive handling — swallowing an unexpected error into a 403 origin would hide a real fault behind a CORS refusal.

findings.title: ADR 0026 D5 still asserts the SameSite premise the same commit's dated correction declares false, and the correction cites D5 as one of the two controls that do not rest on it
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Duty 3, the docs-only commit c0181b01 the brief asked me to verify rather than mutate. THE CORRECTION ITSELF IS TRUE, and I verified both halves against the code and the deployment map. (a) The premise fix is right: production is https://repworth.net (deployment-guide.md:57,177,444,525,1261) and the Admin app is https://admin.repworth.net / https://admin.staging.repworth.net (env-vars.md:48), so the two share the registrable domain repworth.net and are schemefully SAME-SITE while being cross-ORIGIN; a lax (and a strict) cookie IS sent on a credentialed fetch between them. (b) Control one resolves: assertSameOrigin (src/lib/shared/csrf.ts:53-81) throws unless isSelfOrigin(origin) matches NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, and it IS wired to the Admin API — not by a direct call, but through withSameOrigin() (src/lib/auth/route-helpers.ts:30), which wraps 55 admin route exports (POST /api/admin/businesses:114, PATCH .../[id]:110, PUT .../keywords:66, POST /api/admin/impersonation/start:119, POST /api/admin/suppressions:59, POST /api/admin/autonomy/unsuspend:45, and the rest). (c) Control two is true as literally written but is not a CSRF control: absent Access-Control-Allow-Credentials the browser blocks the RESPONSE, and CSRF does not need to read the response — the state change has already happened. The control that actually does that work is D4 (src/proxy.ts:150-157 refuses a non-allowlisted Origin with 403 before any Supabase call), which the correction does not name. THE DEFECT: ADR 0026 D5 (:206-211) restates the corrected premise verbatim — 'SameSite is the second control: rw_impersonation is strict and every other cookie is lax, so no cookie reaches a cross-origin fetch in the first place' — and that sentence is FALSE for the exact topology this ADR is written for. The correction was applied to the Context bullet only, and then cited D5 as a control 'that do[es] not rest on the false premise' while D5's own text names SameSite as its second control. Net effect of c0181b01: the ADR is now internally contradictory, and the uncorrected instance sits in a LOCKED decision rather than in Context. Rated P1, not P0, deliberately: the sentence is supporting rationale, not a normative rule; D5's normative rule ('Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is never sent') is correct, implemented and pinned by R19/R20; the false sentence is unchanged since the merge base and no code depends on it; and the ADR's overall CSRF conclusion does hold, via D4 plus withSameOrigin. An arbiter reading Duty 3's letter ('a misleading FALSE claim is P0') could rate it higher. Remedy: extend the same dated correction to D5 (or delete D5's SameSite sentence and name D4 in its place), and add D4 to the correction's list of surviving controls. Sibling search recorded: the only other SameSite claim in an ADR is 0024:42-47, which says 'a cross-SITE response cannot set it' — correctly scoped, and about setting rather than sending. Zero other siblings.

findings.title: Three durable docs still state the PRE-FIX predicate `isProductionEnvironment() === (VERCEL_TARGET_ENV === 'production')`; round 2's RT-11 fix corrected the plan only, and the directory-map row's stated reason for rejecting requiresProductionConfig() is now the exact imprecision the new fallback accepts
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Duty 3, re-resolved at c0181b01. The plan IS fixed — plan.md:96-99 now spells the two-branch predicate with the NODE_ENV fallback and D-1 (:226-235) cites by symbol, so round-2 RT-11 is closed. Three other durable docs were not updated in the same pass and each states something false at HEAD, where src/lib/config/flags.ts:83-87 is `const target = VERCEL_TARGET_ENV?.trim(); if (target) return target === 'production'; return NODE_ENV === 'production'`. (1) .claude/reference/env-vars.md:48 — a row this branch ADDED — says loopback is 'refused in the production lane (`VERCEL_TARGET_ENV === "production"`, via `isProductionEnvironment()`)'. This is the worst of the three: it is not merely stale, it is self-contradictory, because the justification it gives for rejecting requiresProductionConfig() (that NODE_ENV=production is true on staging) is precisely the imprecision isProductionEnvironment now accepts on its fallback branch, and flags.ts:65-71 says so in its own JSDoc. Neither is what the code does: the predicate consults NODE_ENV once the precise signal fails, and on a missing signal it fails closed only when NODE_ENV is production. Rated P1 and not P0 on the same basis round 2 rated RT-11: the shipped code and its JSDoc are correct and R1-R6 pin all of it, so no reader acting on the CODE produces a defect; the risk is a future engineer 'restoring' the stated equality, which is exactly the shape that produced the wrong A1 fix in the first place. Blast radius re-checked: isProductionEnvironment still has exactly ONE caller in the whole repo (src/lib/config/admin-origins.ts:188), and process.env.VERCEL now has ZERO production readers (grep over src/, worker/, scripts/ — only two dead `delete process.env.VERCEL` lines survive in flags.test.ts:71,101). findings.title: The rewritten Edge-safety extractor closes every literal-quote shape but still cannot see a specifier split below the `node:` prefix — `import('node' + ':crypto')` walks through
findings.arbiter_reasoning:
Duty 1/2, and the residual after RT-14. The backtick fix is real and I proved it five ways: R7 (the verbatim round-2 R4 template literal), R9 (a nested `${}` substitution — extracted as 'node:${', which still trips the prefix match), R8 (a concatenation ABOVE the prefix, `'node:' + 'crypto'` — extracted as 'node:'), R10 (`export … from`), R11 (`import type … from`) all now FAIL the assertion, and R14 confirms protected-routes.ts joined the scanned graph. The one shape left is R12: `import('node' + ':crypto')`, split BELOW the scheme prefix, which yields the harmless specifier 'node'. ARBITER REASONING for not calling this a confirmed survivor: the mutant is genuinely not behaviour-preserving (the module really does import a node builtin), so it is not `equivalent`; but the four regexes are a lexical extractor over QUOTED LITERAL specifiers, and a computed specifier is not one — no regex over source text can see it, so there is no one-character remedy of RT-14's kind. That makes it a claim about the ORACLE's domain rather than about the mutant, which is the class round 2 assigned INV-206, and it forces INCOMPLETE_ORACLE. Rated P2 rather than P1 (round 2 rated RT-14 P1): a backtick specifier is a shape a reviewer would plausibly write and the fix left it unstated, whereas a concatenated dynamic import is not a shape that occurs anywhere in this repo and is visibly outside what the extractor's own code claims. Cheapest honest remedy, and the one that also resolves the inventory row: extend the sibling test at :251 ('scans direct specifiers only — the depth-1 limit is stated, not implied') to state the LEXICAL limit as well — the scan reads quoted literal specifiers, so a computed one is out of scope by construction. That converts INV-312 from an unstated gap into an `excluded` row against a stated scope. A stricter alternative — banning `import(` with a non-literal argument in the graph files — is a real option but is scope this ticket did not buy.

--- ROUND-3 VERIFIER RE-STAMP (2026-09-08, verification only, no mutation) ---
The orchestrator's move of INV-312 from inconclusive/oracle to `excluded` is FAITHFUL and the class is RIGHT, and I am the row's author saying so. Faithful: the row's reason preserves the original survival verdict verbatim before recording the move, names who made it, and records the stricter alternative as NOT taken — no evidence is hidden, and a reader still learns that R12 survived. Right: the SKILL's status rule turns on an IN-SCOPE inconclusive row, and `excluded` is the outcome that records "out of scope, with the reason on the row". What changed is not the mutant but the oracle's declared domain: admin-origins.test.ts:259 now states the lexical limit in the guard's own suite — quoted literal specifiers only, a computed one out of scope by construction, the guard aimed at the accident rather than at deliberate obfuscation. That declaration is now permanent in the codebase rather than only in this report, which is the whole point. One caveat recorded rather than waived: `excluded` normally means "never executed"; INV-312 WAS executed and its mutant survived. The row's reason makes that unmissable, so the classification is a scope statement, not a concealment. Verified at 7ae59bed with the covering suite green (151/151, unchanged).

findings.title: The Edge-safety graph gained src/lib/shared/protected-routes.ts but src/lib/auth/flags.ts, the proxy's third repo-code direct import, is still unscanned
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Duty 4, recorded sibling search. Scope: src/proxy.ts's direct repo-code imports (:3-17), compared against the `graph` array at admin-origins.test.ts:203-209. src/proxy.ts imports four repo modules — @/lib/shared/protected-routes, @/lib/shared/request-path-header, @/lib/auth/flags, @/lib/config/admin-origins. `graph` now lists five paths and covers two of those four plus src/lib/config/flags.ts and src/lib/shared/csrf.ts (both reached one hop deeper, through admin-origins.ts). R13 demonstrates the consequence — a node:crypto import added to src/lib/auth/flags.ts reaches the Edge proxy and the guard does not see it — and the row is `equivalent` with a proof, exactly as round 2 recorded the identical demonstration against protected-routes.ts. Risk today is genuinely small and I am not overstating it: request-path-header.ts is two exported string constants with zero imports, and auth/flags.ts imports only @/lib/config/flags, which IS scanned. So this is P2 and NOT a regression: the fix pass closed the instance round 2 filed (RT-15) and left the class open. Exclusions recorded: external specifiers (next/server, @supabase/ssr) are deliberately out of scope per the depth-1 sibling test at :251, and I did not extend the search past depth 1. findings.title: The RT-17/RT-10 fix DELETED `delete process.env.VERCEL` from admin-origins.test.ts's withEnv instead of retargeting it, so three suites' unset-lane assertions now hang on an ambient NODE_ENV that vitest only defaults with `??=`
findings.arbiter_reasoning:
Duty 2, environment dependence — the same hazard round 2 filed as RT-17, transferred from VERCEL to NODE_ENV by the fix that closed it. The removed line was explicit hygiene; what replaced it is a comment (:34-37) whose premise is 'Vitest sets NODE_ENV=test'. Vitest does not set it — it DEFAULTS it: node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/cli-api.C6CiCDM3.js:14567 is `process.env.NODE_ENV ??= "test"`, so a developer shell exporting NODE_ENV=production keeps production. Unlike RT-17, assertions depend on this TODAY and I measured it rather than argued it: R21 flips the fallback to `true` and admin-origins.test.ts's loopback case fails with 'http://localhost @ lane=undefined: expected false to be true' — the lane=undefined iteration (admin-origins.test.ts:168-190) resolves through the fallback, as does flags.test.ts:71-73's opening assertion. proxy.test.ts is immune only by accident: both its loopback cases set VERCEL_TARGET_ENV explicitly (:439 'staging', :450 'production'), an affirmative signal that short-circuits the fallback. Rated P2, not P1, on the failure DIRECTION: a stray NODE_ENV=production makes these suites fail loudly, never pass while broken, so it is a false-alarm hazard and not a coverage lie; and CI does not set NODE_ENV=production. Remedy, matching the shape of the line that was deleted: `Object.assign(process.env, { NODE_ENV: 'test' })` in withEnv and in proxy.test.ts's beforeEach — @types/node types NODE_ENV read-only, which is why the assign form, and flags.test.ts already uses exactly that spelling at :103. While there: flags.test.ts:71 and :101 still `delete process.env.VERCEL` for a variable nothing reads any more.

--- ROUND-3 VERIFIER RE-STAMP (2026-09-08, verification only, no mutation) ---
FIXED AT THE SITE THIS FINDING CITES, and I accept the disposition — but the fix is PARTIAL against the remedy this finding wrote, and that is recorded rather than smoothed over. Done: withEnv now does `Object.assign(process.env, { NODE_ENV: 'test' })` (admin-origins.test.ts:40), which closes the 13 cases in the file the `at` field names, including the lane=undefined loopback iteration R21 used to prove the dependence was live. NOT done: this finding's remedy also named `proxy.test.ts`'s beforeEach, which is unchanged — immune today only because both its loopback cases set VERCEL_TARGET_ENV explicitly, exactly as the finding says. Also unchanged and still ambient-dependent: flags.test.ts's opening assertion in `isProductionEnvironment is true only for VERCEL_TARGET_ENV=production`, which deletes the target env and asserts false BEFORE the test sets NODE_ENV itself. So an exported NODE_ENV=production in a developer's shell still fails that one suite. Disposition kept `fixed` because the cited defect is repaired, the severity is P2 (never blocking), and the failure direction is loud rather than silent — it can produce a false alarm, never a false pass. Recommended one-line follow-up, not a reopened finding: the same Object.assign in flags.test.ts's afterEach/opening and in proxy.test.ts's beforeEach.
